features.description: Parse urn:ankusa:claim:v1:<tenant>:<claim_id> into tenant_id, claim_id, and the /v1/claims/{tenant_id}/{claim_id} path; anything else raises InvalidClaimRefError.

Parse urn:ankusa:claim:v2:<tenant>:<claim_id>:<exp_unix>:<signature> (exp_unix: decimal, 1-12 digits, no leading zero; signature: 43 unpadded base64url characters) into the same tenant_id and claim_id, with the path /v1/claims/{tenant_id}/{claim_id}?exp={exp_unix}&sig={signature}. The SDK never verifies the signature: the gateway does. Any other segment count, exp or signature shape, or version raises InvalidClaimRefError; a message's claim in either form passes the same parse.

Redeeming a v2 ref requests the path with its ?exp=&sig= query exactly as parse_claim_ref returns it; the gateway's 400 bad_signature and 410 ref_expired are ClaimRejectedError(status, body), and 503 overloaded is ClaimCheckUnavailableError (retryable).
GET /v1/claims/{tenant_id}/{claim_id} and return the body bytes verbatim (text, binary, empty).
A malformed ref, or a sha256 that isn't 64 lowercase hex chars, raises InvalidClaimRefError before any request is made.
Returned bytes are verified against the expected sha256; a mismatch raises ClaimIntegrityError.

404 -> ClaimNotFoundError; 408 and 429 -> ClaimCheckUnavailableError (retryable, like 5xx); other 4xx -> ClaimRejectedError(status, body); 5xx, any other non-200, an unfollowed redirect, or no connection -> ClaimCheckUnavailableError (retryable).
GET /health returns the JSON body on 200; anything else raises ClaimCheckUnavailableError.
Client-level headers ride on every request.
A per-client request timeout; exceeding it raises ClaimCheckUnavailableError.
An injectable transport (Python transport=, TypeScript fetch) replaces the network.
Parse x-ankusa-id/-source/-tenant/-dedupe-key/-replay-id/-idempotency-key and content-type case-insensitively; a missing or empty x-ankusa-id raises MissingHookIdError.
Decode a v1 queue message: the inline (body_base64) and claim body forms, the optional fields (sha256, dedupe_key, replay_id, idempotency_key, headers), and unknown keys are ignored.

A v1 queue message carries the hook's W3C trace context as the optional string fields traceparent and tracestate (null or absent decodes to null), so a consumer continues the trace Ankusa started. Either field present but neither a string nor null -> InvalidMessageError(invalid_field, field = that key). The SDK passes the strings through verbatim: it does not parse or validate the traceparent.
Size mismatch -> InvalidMessageError(size_mismatch); sha256 mismatch -> InvalidMessageError(integrity); claim tenant != tenant_id -> InvalidMessageError(tenant_mismatch).

The idempotency key: the message's idempotency_key field (or the x-ankusa-idempotency-key header) when present; otherwise computed as tenant:source_id:dedupe_key (tenant 'default' when null) for a non-empty dedupe_key, else id. With include_replay and a replay_id, append #replay:<replay_id>.

Verify a Standard Webhooks signature: webhook-signature holds space-separated v1,<base64> entries, each an HMAC-SHA256 over <webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<body> with one configured secret (whsec_ + base64 key, or the raw UTF-8 bytes of any other string); any matching entry for any secret passes (constant-time compare); webhook-timestamp must be within tolerance_seconds (default 300) of now. Header names are case-insensitive. Returns the id and the timestamp.

Failures raise InvalidSignatureError(retryable=false, code, field), checked in this order: no secret, or a whsec_ secret whose remainder is not valid base64 -> invalid_secret (field null); a missing or empty webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature (in that order) -> missing_header (field = that header); a timestamp that is not all decimal digits -> invalid_timestamp; |now - timestamp| > tolerance -> timestamp_out_of_tolerance (both field webhook-timestamp); no matching v1 entry (other versions are ignored) -> no_matching_signature (field webhook-signature).

A webhook-signature header may carry Ed25519 (v1a,<base64>) entries beside the HMAC (v1,<base64>) ones, as the Standard Webhooks specification allows. An HMAC verifier (verify_signature) ignores every entry that is not v1,: a delivery whose valid v1 entry sits beside a v1a one verifies, and one that carries only v1a entries is no_matching_signature, never a pass. The vector is the specification's reference message signed with the RFC 8032 test key 1 (public key whpk_11qYAYKxCrfVS/7TyWQHOg7hcvPapiMlrwIaaPcHURo=), which Ankusa core's Verifier.Asymmetric verifies from the same bytes (packages/ankusa/test/ankusa/verifier_test.exs).

A receiver of Ankusa's HTTP sink (receive_delivery) requires a signature by default. With secrets configured it verifies the delivery exactly as verify_signature does and answers InvalidSignatureError (a 401) for a missing or bad signature; allow_unsigned does not weaken a configured secret. With no secrets and no allow_unsigned it refuses every delivery with InvalidSignatureError(invalid_secret, field null), so an unconfigured receiver is never open. allow_unsigned: true with no secrets accepts a delivery unverified (verified=false). The signature is checked before the hook id: a delivery with no x-ankusa-id raises MissingHookIdError only once it passed (or was allowed to skip) the signature check. Success returns the parsed delivery headers plus verified.
Create, list, read, replace, update, and delete route definitions over the route-management listener (routes.admin.port).
Get and replace the global IP rules.
Dry-run a request against the route table and return the decision without capturing anything.

2xx is success. 404 -> RouteNotFoundError; every other 4xx -> RoutesRejectedError(status, code = the body's error, field, message, conflicting_id, max_routes, scope = the body's scope when present, else null). Anything else that isn't 2xx (5xx, an unfollowed 3xx redirect, 1xx), a transport failure, or a non-JSON success body -> RoutesUnavailableError (retryable).

Route ids are checked before any request and then percent-encoded as one path segment: an id that isn't a string, is empty, or is exactly `.` or `..` raises InvalidRouteIdError (no request), while every other id travels with `/`, `?`, `#`, `%` and space escaped as %2F %3F %23 %25 %20.
Requests match the documented API: JSON bodies carry exactly the caller's input, and query parameters go out in input order with booleans as `true`/`false`.
GET /health on the route-management listener returns {status, routes}.
Operator API: health, Prometheus metrics, redacted config, DLQ list, replay jobs, and quarantine.

GET /v1/audit on the operator API: the audit trail, newest first, paged by cursor/limit and filtered by since, until, actor, action, tenant (query parameters in input order, only those given). Returns {entries, next_cursor}; errors as admin.errors.

2xx is success. A 409 whose body has error role_not_enabled -> RoleNotEnabledError(role); every other 4xx -> AdminRejectedError(status, code = the body's error, scope = the body's scope when present, else null). Anything else that isn't 2xx (5xx, an unfollowed 3xx redirect, 1xx) or a transport failure -> AdminUnavailableError (retryable).

A queue message says how the hook was verified at ingest. decode_message exposes the message's verification object ({status, flagged}; null when the message predates the field or says null; a present value that is not an object of a non-empty string status and a boolean flagged is InvalidMessageError(invalid_field, field verification)). status is ok, failed or skipped; the SDK does not reject other values. trusted answers whether the decoded message may be treated as verified: true only for status ok with flagged false; a flagged message (accepted despite a failed check, on_verify_failure: accept_flag), a failed or skipped one, any other status, and a message with no verification are untrusted.

An HTTP-sink delivery says how the hook was verified at ingest. parse_headers exposes x-ankusa-verification as {status: <value>, flagged: <x-ankusa-verification-flagged == "true">}, null when the header is absent or empty; receive_delivery returns the same object. status is ok, failed or skipped; the SDK does not reject other values. trusted answers whether the parsed headers may be treated as verified: true only for status ok with flagged false; a flagged delivery, a failed or skipped one, any other status, and one with no verification header are untrusted. This is separate from the signature check of receive_delivery (webhook.require_signature): that proves the sink signed the delivery, this says how the node verified the provider's request.

An SDK accepts every queue message whose v is an integer from min_supported to max_supported inclusive (1 and 2) and maps each version to its one current message type: decode_message reports the wire v it read, and the rest of the decode (rules, order, result) is the same for every accepted version. supported_versions returns {min, max}, the two bounds the SDK exposes (constants or functions in the SDK's idiom). A v outside the range, missing, or not an integer -> InvalidMessageError(unsupported_version, field null, retryable false): the permanent failure a consumer dead-letters, never retries.

v 2 is defined as v 1 plus additive fields: a v 2 message decodes exactly like the v 1 message with the same known fields, whatever extra keys it carries (unknown keys of any JSON type are ignored), with v = 2 in the result; a v 2 message is validated by the v 1 rules, so a bad field is the same InvalidMessageError.

A queue message names where it was published from: instance (the Ankusa instance's name) and region (the instance's configured region). decode_message exposes both as a string, null when the message says null or lacks the key (a node older than the fields); a present value that is neither a string nor null is InvalidMessageError(invalid_field, field = that key). They are checked after tracestate, instance first.

The messages Ankusa core itself writes decode as expected. The cases in cases/producer.json are generated by `mix ankusa.conformance.gen` from Ankusa.Sink.Message.encode/3 (inline, claim, replay and ordered, flagged and unverified hooks, with and without a configured region) and are never edited by hand; check.mjs regenerates them and fails when the checked-in file differs, so a field added to the encoder without a vector update fails the gate, and every SDK must decode what the encoder writes.

An HTTP-sink delivery says when the edge accepted the hook and the SHA-256 of the body it sent: parse_headers and receive_delivery return received_at (the x-ankusa-received-at header, unix milliseconds: 1 to 15 decimal digits, as an integer) and body_sha256 (x-ankusa-body-sha256: exactly 64 lowercase hex characters, as is). Both are advisory and optional: a header that is absent, empty or malformed (not digits, too long, uppercase or short hex) is null, never an error, so a sender older than the headers still parses.

Every failure a consumer's decoders raise for a message that cannot be read (decode_message, decode_lifecycle) or a delivery that cannot be trusted (receive_delivery's signature check) carries retryable=false, so a consumer sends it to its terminal queue instead of requeueing the same bytes forever: invalid_json (empty or truncated included), not_an_object, unsupported_version (a v above the SDK's maximum, a specversion other than 1.0), invalid_field. check.mjs also fails any case that expects InvalidMessageError or InvalidSignatureError without retryable=false. The policy: docs/delivery.md, Consumer failure policy.

decode_lifecycle decodes a lifecycle event (a CloudEvents 1.0 structured-mode event: the decoded body of a message the lifecycle sinks publish, content type application/cloudevents+json) into specversion, id, source, type, subject, time, datacontenttype, data, revision, actor, instance, sequence, replayid, traceparent, tracestate. Not JSON -> invalid_json; not an object -> not_an_object; specversion missing or not "1.0" -> unsupported_version; id, source, type, subject, time not non-empty strings, data present but neither an object nor null, revision neither null/absent nor an integer >= 1, sequence neither null/absent nor a string of decimal digits, or datacontenttype, actor, instance, replayid, traceparent, tracestate neither a string, null nor absent -> invalid_field with field = the key, checked in the order listed in conformance/README.md (first failure wins). Unknown keys and unknown types are ignored; absent optional fields decode to null.
